note: Large forested MDC area south-west of Kirksville with ten small gravel parking lots, lettered A to J on the area map, each marked for primitive camping; camping is on or beside the lot. Lot A on Route N is the horse camp; lots F and G are generator-free. A privy stands at the shooting range (lot C), and none at the camping lots. Hiking and horse trails throughout. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: lot camping that MDC designates at all ten lots (map Primitive Camping symbol beside every Parking Lot A-J; GIS camping points at each; brochure 'on or adjacent to all area parking lots and in designated camping areas') - stays under the Lick Creek reading of the lot rule, flagged for the owner. No built campground anywhere on imagery. PIN MOVE proposed from lot G (a tiny pull-in among private houses) to lot H. Acreage corrected out of the note. Phone matches.
flags: LOT RULE - STAYS, OWNER TO CONFIRM: the brochure says 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all area parking lots and in designated camping areas.', 'Camping with horses/pack animals is only allowed at parking lot A.', 'No unattended open campfires allowed.' and 'Walk-in/backpack camping is allowed EXCEPT during firearms deer and turkey seasons.' The 12/4/2018 map puts a Primitive Camping symbol beside each of the ten lettered Parking Lot symbols and notes 'Parking Lot A is for Horse Camping; Parking Lot G and F are Generator Free'. GIS layer 27 has 16 'Primitive Camping Area' points, all at those ten lots (five stacked at lot H, three at lot J, one at each of the rest). I viewed every lot: each is a bare gravel pad, from about 12 x 10 m (G) to about 45 x 20 m (A), with no pads, rings, tables or loops; there is no separate built camp. Designated points at the lots keep it under the Lick Creek reading. This is the largest of the batch's lot-camping areas, so the owner's call here sets the others.

PIN MOVE: stored 40.10604,-92.60532 is lot G at the north-east corner: a pull-in about 12 x 10 m at a road junction with private houses 30-60 m away on three sides, and generator-free. Proposed 40.10293,-92.60785, lot H on Foghorn Trail, 400 m south-west: a gravel pad about 30 x 20 m at a bend of the gravel road inside the forest, where GIS stacks five camping points (the most of any lot). Alternatives with more room: lot B 40.10946,-92.65028 (about 40 x 15 m, directly off paved Route N) and lot J 40.12429,-92.65792 (three GIS points, off the gravel road at the north-west corner).

HORSE CAMP: lot A (40.11869,-92.63955, on paved Route N) is the designated horse camp; it is 3.2 km from the pin and the other nine lots are horse-free for camping, so the entry is not a horse camp. The trails are shared hiking/biking/equestrian.
NO SPLIT: the ten lots are spread over 5 km on different roads, but each is a single small lot. Nothing else in the database within 4 km.
ACREAGE: the stored note said 2,603 acres (the 2018 map says 2,602); the area page now says 3,081.5. The figure is out of the new note.
ALERT: the page carries 'The Shooting Range will be closed until further notice.' The range is at lot C, 4 km from the pin; no camping closure is posted.

ACCESS: lots A, B and C are off paved Route N, the rest off gravel county roads (Crest Trail, Foghorn Trail, Sugar Creek School Trail). No posted limit or 4WD wording on the page, brochure or map. The GIS lot records all read 'Surface: Paved, Allows_Trailers: No', which is plainly a default (every lot is gravel on imagery) and was not used.
PHONE: stored 660-785-2420 matches the page's 'For more information call (660) 785-2420'.
Stored year_round (manual) stands; the seasonal limit is on walk-in camping only.
